title: Ciena Outlines Strong 2027 Outlook: What's Fueling the Momentum?
author: Na
description: Ciena Corporation reported Q3 revenue growth of 37% and adjusted EPS surge of 215%, driven by strong AI network spending. The company's backlog exceeded $10 billion with most demand for 2027, and it projects at least 30% revenue growth in fiscal 2027. Competitors Corning and Viavi Solutions are also benefiting from AI infrastructure and data center investments.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong Q3 results with 37% revenue growth and 215% EPS surge. Robust $10B+ backlog predominantly for 2027, secured supply chain through 2029, and guidance of at least 30% fiscal 2027 revenue growth demonstrate sustained momentum from AI-driven optical demand and market leadership.

Benefiting from AI infrastructure and optical connectivity demand. Management targets $20B annualized sales run rate by end of 2026, with ambitious goals of $30B by 2028 and $40B by 2030, supported by AI infrastructure and solar expansion.

Sustained demand across data centers, AI infrastructure, and aerospace/defense markets driving NSE business growth. Q1 fiscal 2027 revenue guidance of $450-460M with strong NSE segment momentum and ~27.1% non-GAAP operating margin.

title: CIEN Q3 Earnings Beat on AI-Led Cloud Demand, Top Line Climbs 37% Y/Y
author: Zacks.Com
description: Ciena Corporation reported strong Q3 fiscal 2026 results with adjusted earnings of $2.11 per share (215% YoY growth) and revenues of $1.67 billion (37% YoY growth), driven by AI-led cloud demand. Cloud provider revenues jumped 82% YoY and represented 53% of total sales. The company raised full-year 2026 guidance to $6.42 billion and projects at least 30% revenue growth for fiscal 2027.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong Q3 earnings beat with 215% YoY EPS growth, 37% revenue growth driven by AI-led cloud demand, significant margin expansion (1,180 bps operating margin improvement), raised full-year guidance, and projects 30%+ growth for fiscal 2027. Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) rating.
Q2 2026 EPS beat consensus by 14 cents (167% YoY improvement), revenues exceeded guidance despite slight YoY decline, demonstrating strong operational performance.
Q2 2026 earnings up 30% YoY, revenues surged 17% and beat consensus, with Enterprise Networks sales jumping 65% driven by AI infrastructure demand.
Q4 fiscal 2026 earnings beat consensus by 13.33%, revenues increased 52.5% YoY driven by data center ecosystem and aerospace/defense demand, with Network segment delivering 70% YoY revenue growth.

title: If a Bear Market Is Coming, This Growth Stock Might Be a Great Buy on the Dip
author: Anthony Di Pizio
description: With the S&P 500 trading at historically high valuations and potential market headwinds ahead, Corning emerges as an attractive opportunity for investors seeking a discount. The company is capitalizing on AI data center demand through its fiber-optic connectivity solutions, with major deals from Meta and Amazon. While currently trading at a P/E of 51.9, the author suggests waiting for a market correction to push the stock toward $100 before buying, where it would trade at a more reasonable 34.7 P/E ratio.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong growth prospects driven by AI data center demand, major contracts with Meta and Amazon, expanding manufacturing capacity, and projected revenue growth from $20B to $40B by 2030. However, current valuation is expensive, making it a better buy on a dip.

Mentioned as the undisputed leader in AI semiconductor hardware with a lower P/E ratio (27.5) compared to Corning, used as a valuation benchmark rather than being the focus of investment recommendation.
Referenced as a major customer of Corning with a $6 billion multiyear deal for optical connectivity solutions, indicating strong AI infrastructure investment but not directly analyzed.
Mentioned as another major customer of Corning with a similar deal signed in June, demonstrating demand for AI data center solutions but not directly evaluated.
Referenced only as a historical customer of Corning's glass products for iPhones, not relevant to the current AI investment thesis.

title: WDAY's Operating Margin Expands: Will the Improvement Continue?
author: Na
description: Workday delivered strong profitability improvements in Q2 with non-GAAP operating margin expanding to 31.1% and subscription revenues growing 13.9%. The company's AI business is gaining momentum with agentic AI ARR reaching $600 million, up 200% year-over-year. Other tech firms like Corning and Sanmina also demonstrated significant margin expansion driven by strong execution and AI infrastructure demand.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong Q2 results with 21% operating income growth, 31.1% non-GAAP operating margin expansion, 13.9% subscription revenue growth, and 200% year-over-year growth in agentic AI ARR. Healthy backlog of $27.4 billion provides visibility into future revenue.

Core operating margin expanded 220 basis points to 20.2% and ROIC improved 190 basis points to 13.5%. Strong growth in Optical Communications segment driven by hyperscale data-center investments and GenAI networking infrastructure demand.

Non-GAAP operating margin expanded significantly from 5.7% to 8.0% with operating income reaching $275.8 million. Improvement driven by strong execution, cost management, and momentum in cloud and AI infrastructure.

title: Meet the Super Semiconductor Stock Crushing Nvidia in 2026
author: Micah Zimmerman
description: Credo Technology (CRDO) has outperformed Nvidia by 80% vs 20% in 2026 by providing critical high-speed connectivity infrastructure for AI data centers. The article highlights how companies supplying the 'plumbing' of AI infrastructure—like Credo's connectivity solutions and Corning's fiber-optic cables—are becoming as important as GPU chips themselves for scaling AI clusters.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Company has crushed Nvidia with 80% YTD gains by providing essential high-speed connectivity infrastructure for AI data centers. Positioned as critical to AI scaling with strong gross margins (68%), large hyperscaler contracts, and vendor-agnostic positioning that benefits from overall AI growth.

While Nvidia remains important for compute, the article frames it as less exciting than infrastructure plays. Up only 20% YTD compared to Credo's 80%, and the narrative suggests infrastructure companies are capturing more value in the AI cycle.

Identified as a quiet winner supplying fiber-optic cables for AI data centers. Meta's $6 billion commitment through 2030 and new multicore fiber products specifically designed for AI data centers demonstrate strong positioning in the infrastructure buildout.
Mentioned as a beneficiary of Credo's vendor-agnostic positioning, but not a primary focus. Credo's success is independent of any single chip vendor's roadmap.
Referenced as a major hyperscaler customer committing significant capital to fiber infrastructure, but not analyzed as an investment opportunity in this article.
